title: A pane screenshot taken while no viewer is on screen shows a frame the app has not redrawn
body:
decade renders a frame for a viewer only after the viewer sends `Ready`. `render_viewers` in `decade/src/server/compositor/viewers.rs` skips any viewer that has not. The viewer sends `Ready` from its `frame` handler in `decade/src/viewer.rs`, which runs only when the host compositor gives it a frame callback. At the end of each render, decade answers the frame callbacks of the windows in visible panes, in `render` in `decade/src/server/compositor/render.rs`.

When Jack switches Hyprland to another workspace, Hyprland stops sending the viewer frame callbacks. decade stops rendering. Every window in decade then waits for a callback that does not come. An app that redraws on its own stops drawing. An eframe app keeps running `App::logic` and stops running `App::ui`, because eframe on Wayland draws only on winit's `RedrawRequested`.

Jack never sees this pause. An agent can. decade renders a pane screenshot through its own path in `decade/src/server/compositor/screenshot.rs`. That path reads the frame back first and answers the callbacks after. In each screenshot an agent takes while Jack is elsewhere, the app's content is no newer than the previous screenshot or the moment Jack left.

An agent working on acre filed this bug from acre-4db16b. It read eframe's trace as decade never sending frame callbacks. Jack had probably switched Hyprland workspaces while it worked.

## Reproduction

A `decade script` viewer stopped with `SIGSTOP` for 4 s stood in for a hidden viewer, since a stopped viewer sends no `Ready`. The server ran with its own `XDG_RUNTIME_DIR` and `XDG_STATE_HOME`, under `WAYLAND_DEBUG=server`. Its ghostty pane ran a `date` loop ten times a second. Counts per second of the server log, from the moment of the stop:

| second | `wl_callback.done` | `wl_surface.commit` |
|---|---|---|
| -2 | 24 | 12 |
| -1 | 19 | 9 |
| 0 | 1 | 1 |
| 1 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 | 2 | 1 |
| 4 | 23 | 11 |

The server sent no `wl_callback.done` for 3962 ms. ghostty committed nothing in that time. Both resumed on `SIGCONT`. The run did not test Hyprland itself withholding callbacks from a window on a hidden workspace.

## Proposal

Before reading back, decade answers the frame callbacks of the pane's window and its popups. It waits for that window to commit, up to a short timeout, and then renders. Rendering for viewers stays as it is. An app that nobody looks at still draws nothing. The same change covers a screenshot of a workspace that no viewer shows.

## Open

- How long to wait for the commit. An idle app commits nothing, and the timeout is then the cost of every screenshot of it.
- Whether to give `decade script` a step that withholds `Ready`. A test could then cover this.
close_reason: Landed in 68ce2dc on dev. The note on this issue has the check against the build before it.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f5ffdd3d
notes.text: Rewritten after a reproduction. The first body blamed the scratch pane. The cause is that decade renders, and so answers frame callbacks, only when a viewer sends Ready, and a viewer on a hidden Hyprland workspace sends none.

notes.author: Jack Roddy/f5ffdd3d
notes.text:
Implemented on `dev` and not yet committed. `capture_fresh` in `decade/src/server/compositor/screenshot.rs` takes the place of both direct `capture` calls. When the pane's window has an unanswered frame callback (`waits_for_frame` in `decade/src/server/compositor.rs`), decade answers it and stores a `Capturing`. The window's next commit completes the capture through `finish_captures`, called from the commit handler. A 200 ms timer completes it otherwise. A window with no pending callback is captured at once, so a screenshot while a viewer is on screen does not wait.

Checked with an isolated server and a `decade script` viewer stopped with `SIGSTOP`. A ghostty pane printed the time twice a second, and a pane screenshot was taken over MCP 5 s after the stop. The build from before the change returned the frame from the moment of the stop. The new build returned the frame from the moment of the request. ghostty committed 0.7 ms after decade answered its callback. The timeout path was not exercised.
